NEW_TERM_TYPE.definition: Industry or sector in which the DLT system is applied, such as education, finance or supply chain.
NEW_TERM_TYPE.evidence: the Blockcerts project, an open source project launched by MIT and Learning Machine in 2016

NEW_TERM_TYPE.definition: Whether the ledger's security relies on quantum information theory or quantum mechanics rather than classical cryptography.
NEW_TERM_TYPE.evidence: its security is guaranteed theoretically by virtue of quantum information theory

NEW_TERM_TYPE.definition: Whether a text proposes or addresses a unified or standardised data model for analysing multiple blockchains.
NEW_TERM_TYPE.evidence: This master's thesis aims at proposing an unified model for blockchain data.

NEW_TERM_TYPE.definition: Application domain in which the DLT is deployed to coordinate, track or verify goods in supply chains.
NEW_TERM_TYPE.evidence: apply institutional cryptoeconomics to the information problems in global trade networks

NEW_TERM_TYPE.definition: Organisational, environmental or technological factors that determine whether an organisation adopts blockchain technology, as studied in adoption models.
NEW_TERM_TYPE.evidence: Whether organizations adopt blockchain technology depends on many factors.

NEW_TERM_TYPE.definition: Whether the distributed ledger is organised in one dimension (single chain) or multiple dimensions (e.g. two-dimensional chain arrangements).
NEW_TERM_TYPE.evidence: The distributed digital ledger may have a plurality of chains of digital blocks in the two-dimensions

crypto_asset_service_type.definition: DLT used for coordinating goods provenance and quality verification rather than financial services.
crypto_asset_service_type.evidence: blockchain will not simply make supply chains more efficient

crypto_asset_function.definition: Blockchain transactions secured by post-quantum (lattice-based) signatures rather than classical cryptography, to resist quantum attack.
crypto_asset_function.evidence: a new lattice-based signature scheme has been proposed, which can be used to secure the blockchain network

ledger_storage_model.proposal: partial or full removal of historical data
ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger design allowing past transaction data to be removed from node storage while cryptographic proofs preserve ledger integrity.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: data of past transactions can be removed from the storage of network nodes based on node permissions

dlt_architecture.definition: Ledger design permitting post-hoc modification or deletion of previously committed blocks while preserving chain linkage via hashes.
dlt_architecture.evidence: a modified block is provided in response to at least an edit transaction that indicates a transaction in an original block

consensus_mechanism.definition: Block generation authority determined by node scores and delegated between blockchain nodes, rather than by a standard consensus rule.
consensus_mechanism.evidence: receiving, by the first blockchain node, a delegation of a block generation authority from a second blockchain node

ledger_access_permission.definition: Ledger membership or access granted to nodes according to the jurisdiction of the recorded event or incident.
ledger_access_permission.evidence: A jurisdiction of the new incident is determined. Nodes that are associated with the jurisdiction are identified.

smart_contract_definition_scope.definition: Smart contract executed in an off-chain test environment with simulated blockchain context and state, rather than on the live ledger.
smart_contract_definition_scope.evidence: performing an off-chain testing on a smart contract
